title: Portability: commit the import event plan through a durable store port
description:
Filed by architect-c9e91335 while planning task-80fce1d1d625453098bd526d61c5ddb8, under the global rail requiring prerequisite production tasks when a claimed capability is measured absent. This is a PRODUCER gap, measured symbol by symbol at HEAD 8222b9e2.

MEASURED GAP. `applyImport` (packages/import/src/import-apply.ts:196) ends by calling `input.store.commit({ aggregateId: `legacy-import:${manifest.digest}`, commandBytes, commandId, committedAt, events, expectedVersion: 0 })` at :219-228, wrapping failure as IMPORT_COMMIT_FAILED / APPLY. So the commit PLAN is production-complete: aggregate id, command identity, committedAt and the `ImportEventDraft[]` (each now carrying `domainSchemaVersion: IMPORT_EVENT_FACTS_VERSION` since task-9745cd06b8004f44af4128f69a251860 landed at import-apply.ts:43,162).

WHAT IS ABSENT is anything that binds that port to a real store:
- `grep -rn "applyImport" apps tools packages --include=*.ts | grep -v '\.test\.'` returns exactly TWO non-test composers: packages/import/src/index.ts:19 (the re-export) and tools/import/import-shadow.ts:141.
- That single composer passes DISCARDING_STORE, defined at tools/import/import-shadow.ts:111 as `commit: () => ({ currentVersion: 0 })`, and the file's own header states "the comparator never sees an authority-bearing store" — by rail, not by accident.
- `grep -rn "@moe/import" apps/daemon/src --include=*.ts | grep -v '\.test\.'` returns ZERO. The daemon does not reference the importer at all.

CONSEQUENCE. No production path has ever written a `legacy.<kind>.imported` event to a SqliteEventStore. The `legacy-import:<manifestDigest>` aggregate is empty in every real deployment, so any durable reader over it correctly answers ABSENT forever, and a shadow comparison against it is vacuous rather than wrong.

DELIVERABLE. One focused production adapter that implements the `ImportStorePort` `commit` shape over a real SqliteEventStore and is invoked on a real import path, so the drafted events become durable rows with their stamped `domainSchemaVersion`. It writes only what `applyImport` drafted — it derives no facts, re-encodes no payload, and adds no event.

NOT IN SCOPE: the durable reader/mapper (task-80fce1d1d625453098bd526d61c5ddb8 owns it), the shadow matrix (task-22cfca91c5134b24aaf3e5734444fb93), activation, cutover, or any dual write. The read-only posture of tools/import/import-shadow.ts is deliberate and must not be changed to satisfy this task — if the durable write belongs behind a daemon command rather than that CLI, say so and place it there.

CONSUMER: task-22cfca91c5134b24aaf3e5734444fb93 needs this to have non-vacuous current-side rows; task-80fce1d1d625453098bd526d61c5ddb8's reader is independently correct without it and is NOT blocked by this task.
definitionOfDone: `grep -rn "applyImport" apps packages --include=*.ts | grep -v '\.test\.'` names a production composer that passes a store port backed by a real SqliteEventStore, where today the only non-test composer passes tools/import/import-shadow.ts:111's DISCARDING_STORE.

The adapter commits exactly the `ImportEventDraft[]` that `applyImport` drafted, at the aggregate id and command identity `applyImport` derived, with `expectedVersion: 0`; a test asserts the durable rows' `domainSchemaVersion` equals IMPORT_EVENT_FACTS_VERSION and that the stored payload bytes are byte-identical to the drafted bytes.
The adapter derives no fact, re-encodes no payload and adds no event: a mutation that re-encodes a payload before committing, or appends one extra event, turns a NAMED test red.

A second commit of the same manifest digest conflicts rather than appending a duplicate aggregate, and the refusal keeps its own exact code and layer rather than being restamped as IMPORT_COMMIT_FAILED; raw event and decision counts prove the original survives.

Real SqliteEventStore tests read the committed rows back through public `decodeImportEventFacts` and assert a nonzero decoded claim count; a store failure surfaces as IMPORT_COMMIT_FAILED / APPLY from `applyImport` itself, asserted by exact code and layer.
Package typecheck and test run with exit codes captured separately and a nonzero `Test Files N passed` count line; only owned paths are committed.
taskRails: Dependency direction is consumer -> @moe/import through public roots only. Never add a dependency from @moe/import toward apps/daemon or @moe/store.
Commit only what applyImport drafted. This adapter is a port implementation, not a producer: no fact derivation, no re-encoding, no extra event, no dual write, no activation, no cutover.

Do not change the read-only posture of tools/import/import-shadow.ts. Its DISCARDING_STORE and 'the comparator never sees an authority-bearing store' header are deliberate; if the durable write belongs behind a daemon command, place it there instead.
Preserve upstream IMPORT_* code and layer verbatim rather than restamping; a store-level conflict is not IMPORT_COMMIT_FAILED.
Use TDD with a real SqliteEventStore, assert exact codes and layers, target <=250 physical lines per production source, and commit only explicit owned paths.

implementationPlan.description: Confirm the measurement and settle PLACEMENT, the one genuinely open decision. Read-only. Re-verify at committed HEAD: (a) `applyImport` (packages/import/src/import-apply.ts:196) commits through `ImportStorePort` at :219-228 with `expectedVersion: 0`, wrapping only THROWN failures as IMPORT_COMMIT_FAILED / APPLY; (b) the only non-test composer is tools/import/import-shadow.ts:141 passing DISCARDING_STORE (:111), whose file header asserts read-only ON BYTES (pre/post digest of every manifest-covered file) -- that posture is rail-protected and must not change; (c) `grep -rn "@moe/import" apps/daemon/src --include=*.ts | grep -v '\.test\.'` returns ZERO. THE SHAPE LUCK THAT MAKES THIS ADAPTER THIN, verify each: `ImportCommitInput` {aggregateId, commandBytes, commandId, committedAt, events, expectedVersion} is field-for-field a subset-compatible shape of the store's `CommitInput` (store-contracts.ts:46-53); `ImportEventDraft` {domainSchemaVersion, eventId, eventType, payload} maps onto the store's `EventDraft` whose `domainSchemaVersion` is OPTIONAL with a generic default (:36-44) -- which is precisely why the import draft made it REQUIRED (import-apply.ts:39-42's own comment: an omitted field persists an envelope schema the stored bytes do not speak). PLACEMENT DECISION, recorded here per the task rail's invitation: the adapter and its CLI entry live in `tools/import/` as a NEW file beside import-shadow.ts -- NOT inside packages/import (the rail forbids @moe/import depending on @moe/store), NOT inside apps/daemon (zero @moe/import references exist there today, and inventing a daemon command kind for import would widen the frozen command vocabulary, a far larger change this task must not smuggle), and NOT inside import-shadow.ts (read-only by rail). tools/ is not a workspace package, so imports are deep relative specifiers with the file named in a root typecheck script -- import-shadow.ts's own header documents this exact precedent and why it does not trip TS6059.

SHAPE LUCK, each verified: ImportCommitInput{aggregateId,commandBytes,commandId,committedAt,events,expectedVersion} (import-apply.ts:49-57) is field-for-field assignable to store CommitInput (store-contracts.ts:46-53). ImportEventDraft.domainSchemaVersion is REQUIRED and literal-typed (:38-47); store EventDraft.domainSchemaVersion is OPTIONAL defaulting to DOMAIN_EVENT_SCHEMA_VERSION (:36-44).

CONFLICT MECHANISM MEASURED FROM SOURCE (step-2 asked for this). packages/store/src/event-ledger-transaction.ts:119-152 `resolveCommand`: it THROWS. Three distinct answers, all reachable from applyImport's deterministic identity —
  1. receipt found AND requestSha256 equal -> returns { disposition: "REPLAYED" }, writes nothing. A byte-identical re-import lands here, NOT on a conflict: commandId = canonicalDigest({manifest,version}) and commandBytes/committedAt/events are all deterministic.
  2. receipt found AND requestSha256 differs -> throws CommandIdConflictError, code "COMMAND_ID_CONFLICT". Reached by the SAME manifest digest with different records (commandId depends only on the digest).
  3. no receipt, previousVersion !== expectedVersion -> throws ExpectedVersionConflictError, "EXPECTED_VERSION_CONFLICT".
Since applyImport's catch restamps every throw, the adapter must CATCH the DurableStoreError, record the store's own `code` verbatim, and rethrow; the composer then answers from the recorded refusal rather than from applyImport's restamped result. Non-conflict throws (closed handle) are recorded as nothing and flow through to IMPORT_COMMIT_FAILED/APPLY — that is the DoD-4/DoD-5 discriminator.

PLACEMENT: tools/import/import-commit.ts as planned, using deep relative `.js` specifiers exactly like its sibling. Bridges confirmed present: packages/import/src/index.js, packages/store/src/sqlite-event-store.js, packages/store/src/store-contracts.js (there is NO packages/store/src/index.js, so the barrel is not reachable that way).

DEPENDENCY EDGE PROBED (rail): a temp tools/import/edge-probe.ts importing BARE @moe/import and @moe/store typechecked exit 0 and was deleted in the same command. Root package.json declares both, pnpm-lock's `.` importer carries both, node_modules/@moe/{import,store} symlinks exist. So the edge exists both ways; the production file still uses relative specifiers for node-runtime parity with import-shadow.ts, while the test uses bare specifiers like tests/integration/portability does.

Root `pnpm test` and `pnpm test:integration` both reach tests/integration/**.

2. "commits rows that decode back to a nonzero claim count through decodeImportEventFacts" — decodes every row through the PUBLIC decoder, asserts a nonzero claim count AND that the decoded legacyIds equal the report's claims' legacyIds, so the assertion is bound to content and not just to a count.
3. "adds no event of its own: the durable ids are exactly the drafted ids" — durable ids equal drafted ids in order, and the RAW event count equals the draft count. Drill-2 target.
4. "replays a byte-identical re-import instead of appending, leaving the rows untouched".
5. "refuses a second import of the same manifest digest with the store's own COMMAND_ID_CONFLICT" — asserts code COMMAND_ID_CONFLICT and layer DURABLE_COMMIT_LAYER, and explicitly `.not.toBe("APPLY")`; raw event AND decision counts plus payload bytes prove the original survived.
6. "surfaces a broken store as IMPORT_COMMIT_FAILED / APPLY from applyImport itself" — closed handle, exact code and exact layer.

CLI: commits a real snapshot into an EXISTING store (buildSourceManifest -> decodeLegacySources -> applyImport over a real temp tree); refuses an absent store path with IMPORT_SOURCE_UNREADABLE/INPUT and asserts `existsSync(path) === false` so nothing was created implicitly; refuses argv naming no store with IMPORT_ROOT_INVALID/INPUT.

MECHANISM SETTLED, from source rather than guessed (event-ledger-transaction.ts:119-152). store.commit THROWS on both conflicts, so the adapter catches DurableStoreError, records the store's own `code` verbatim with layer "STORE", and rethrows; the composer answers from that record, so the conflict is never restamped. A non-conflict throw is recorded as nothing and reaches applyImport's catch as IMPORT_COMMIT_FAILED/APPLY. Test 5 vs test 6 is that discriminator, pinned by exact code AND exact layer on both sides.

ALSO MEASURED, and it changes what test 4 can claim: a byte-identical re-import does NOT conflict. commandId is canonicalDigest({manifest,version}) and commandBytes/committedAt/events are deterministic, so requestSha256 matches and the store answers disposition REPLAYED, writing nothing. Test 4 pins that as REPLAYED; the genuine conflict (test 5) is the same manifest digest with DIFFERENT records, which is what makes commandId collide against a different requestSha256.

Store handles are closed in afterEach (a held SQLite handle kills the vitest worker) and every temp root is removed.

implementationPlan.description: GREEN. Create tools/import/import-commit.ts: the durable `ImportStorePort` implementation plus a minimal CLI entry. The port maps ImportCommitInput -> the store's CommitInput field-for-field: same aggregateId, same commandBytes, same commandId, same committedAt, same expectedVersion, and each ImportEventDraft passed through with its REQUIRED domainSchemaVersion preserved -- no spread-with-defaults that could let the store's generic version leak in, no re-encoding of any payload (pass the Uint8Array through untouched), no derived fact, no added event. THE WHOLE ADAPTER IS THE ABSENCE OF TRANSFORMATION, and the DoD's mutation drills exist to prove that absence. Handle the conflict path per the step-2 measurement: surface the store's own conflict code/layer distinctly from a thrown infrastructure failure. The CLI entry composes buildSourceManifest -> decodeLegacySources -> applyImport with THIS port over a real store path given by flag, prints one JSON report, and refuses to run against a store path that does not exist (fail closed; never create a store implicitly). Add the file to the root `typecheck:import` script alongside import-shadow.ts and shadow-input.ts -- that script enumerates files explicitly, so a new file NOT added is silently untypechecked, the exact class the integration-tests-typechecked-by-nothing gotcha records. Keep the production file <=250 physical lines.
implementationPlan.note:
GREEN. `npx vitest run tests/integration/import` -> Test Files 1 passed (1), Tests 9 passed (9), EXIT=0. `pnpm typecheck:import` EXIT=0. `npx tsc -p tests/integration/import/tsconfig.json` EXIT=0.

SPLIT, forced by the per-FILE line target. One file came out at 278 physical lines, over the <=250 target, so it is two files along the seam its sibling already uses (import-shadow.ts + shadow-input.ts):
- tools/import/durable-import-store.ts (140 lines) — the port and `commitLegacyImport`.
- tools/import/import-commit.ts (158 lines) — argv, the store open, the CLI report, the main guard.

THE ADAPTER IS ONE LINE OF MAPPING, and that is the point. `const commitInput: CommitInput = input;` then `store.commit(commitInput)`. `ImportCommitInput` IS a `CommitInput` structurally, so there is no field list to drift, no spread, no default, no re-encode, no copy. `ImportEventDraft.domainSchemaVersion` is required and literal-typed, so the store's optional generic default can never be the one persisted.

CONFLICT HANDLING as measured in step 1. `durablePort` catches, and only if `cause instanceof DurableStoreError && CONFLICT_CODES.includes(cause.code)` (COMMAND_ID_CONFLICT, EXPECTED_VERSION_CONFLICT) records `{code: cause.code, layer: "STORE"}` — the code is COPIED off the error, never minted — then RETHROWS so applyImport cannot report a success it did not have. `commitLegacyImport` consults that record BEFORE applyImport's result, so the store's code and layer survive instead of being restamped IMPORT_COMMIT_FAILED/APPLY. Any other throw records nothing and is reported by applyImport itself, which is exactly the DoD-4/DoD-5 split. Success returns the store's own `disposition` verbatim as the outcome, so a REPLAY is never dressed up as a fresh commit.

THREE CORRECTIONS THE TYPECHECKER AND NODE FORCED, each proving a gate that would otherwise have been fictional:
1. `ImportedClaim` has NO `legacyId` — it is {claimId, principal, provenance, status}. The decode test asserted `.legacyId`, vitest passed it as undefined === undefined, and only `tsc -p tests/integration/import/tsconfig.json` caught it (TS2339 x2). Now asserts `claimId`. This is precisely the "integration tests are typechecked by nothing" class; the directory tsconfig is why it was caught here rather than by QA.
2. A plain-node run of the CLI failed with ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND on `./durable-import-store.js`. Node does not rewrite .js->.ts; vitest and tsc both do, so the suite was green while the tool was unrunnable. Added `tools/import/durable-import-store.js` (`export * from "./durable-import-store.ts";`), byte-identical in shape to the tracked `tools/import/shadow-input.js` bridge (verified with cmp).
3. `parseOptions` dropped a redundant `flags.size !== 2` check that `args.length !== 5` already implies.

- absent store path -> EXIT 1, {"code":"IMPORT_SOURCE_UNREADABLE","layer":"INPUT",...} and existsSync(path) === false, so nothing was created implicitly.

implementationPlan.description: Mutation drills, the two DoD 3 names plus the vacuity guard. Drill 1 (no re-encoding): make the adapter re-encode one payload (decode + re-serialise) before committing; the step-2 byte-identity test must go RED on the byte comparison, not on a crash. Drill 2 (no extra event): make the adapter append one synthetic event to the drafted list; a NAMED test must go RED on the exact event count and the decoded claim count. Drill 3 (the decode assertion is real): empty the fixture so applyImport drafts zero claim events; the step-2 happy-path test must go RED on its nonzero-decoded-claims assertion -- if it stays green, the assertion is not actually gating on decoded content and must be strengthened. Record for each drill the command, the failing test NAME and the exact assertion. Restore by re-editing, never `git checkout` (destructive in the shared worktree), confirm `git diff --numstat` shows 0 added 0 deleted per drilled file, one drill at a time.

No assertion can separate it, so the drill indicts itself, not the test.

DRILL 2 — append one synthetic event (`{...first, eventId: first.eventId + "-extra"}`). RED, 4 failed | 5 passed, including both DoD-named guards: "adds no event of its own: the durable ids are exactly the drafted ids" -> expected […(3)] to deeply equal […(2)]; "commits rows that decode back to a nonzero claim count…" -> the decoded claim list, 3 against 2; the happy path on row count 3 vs 2; and the CLI's committedEvents.
DRILL 3a — the vacuity drill the plan named: empty the fixture so applyImport drafts zero events. RED, 4 failed | 5 passed, but NOT where the plan predicted, and the reason matters. The happy path reddens on `expect(drafts.length).toBeGreaterThan(0)` -> "expected 0 to be greater than 0", the generated-case guard. The nonzero-decoded-claims assertion is live, and the drill doubles as proof that the adapter must not rewrite the aggregate id applyImport derived.

That is the restamping the DoD forbids, caught by exact code, and the ordering of those two lines is the whole mechanism.

implementationPlan.description: Adversarial review, commit, gate. ATTACKER PASS: can any payload byte differ between draft and row -- including via a defensive copy that normalises, a TextEncoder round-trip, or `.slice()` consulting Symbol.species on hostile input? Does the adapter ever supply a default domainSchemaVersion? Can the CLI write anywhere except the explicitly-flagged store path? Did import-shadow.ts change AT ALL (it must not -- diff it against HEAD to prove zero bytes moved)? Is the conflict path distinguishable from infrastructure failure by code AND layer, and does neither get restamped? Is the new file in the typecheck:import script? DEPENDENCY-DIRECTION CHECK per the rail: packages/import must gain NO import of @moe/store -- grep it. COMMIT: `git status --porcelain`, unstage foreign entries, commit ONLY tools/import/import-commit.ts, its test file, and the package.json script line by explicit pathspec; verify with `git show --stat`. GATE, per DoD 6 with exit codes captured SEPARATELY (never `;`-chained, never piped): `pnpm typecheck:import` then `pnpm typecheck` then the test command for wherever the suite landed -- each must print its own nonzero `Test Files N passed` count line where applicable; a leg with no count line ran nothing. In the completion note name task-22cfca91c5134b24aaf3e5734444fb93 as the consumer this de-vacuates and state that task-80fce1d1's reader is independently correct and was never blocked by this task, exactly as the description records.
implementationPlan.note:
ATTACKER PASS, item by item.
- PAYLOAD BYTES: the adapter performs NO copy, NO slice, NO TextEncoder round trip and NO defensive normalisation — `store.commit(input)` receives the drafted value itself, so there is no site where Symbol.species or a normalising copy could act. The only copy is the store's own `snapshotCommitInput`, which is upstream of my diff and unchanged. Drill 1b proves the byte assertion sees a difference when one exists.
- DEFAULT ENVELOPE: no spread over events anywhere, so `DOMAIN_EVENT_SCHEMA_VERSION` can never displace the draft's required literal `domainSchemaVersion`. Type-enforced, not just intended.
- WRITE SURFACE: the CLI writes only to the operator-named store path (plus SQLite's own -wal/-shm beside it). buildSourceManifest and decodeLegacySources are read-only, and NOTHING is written to the snapshot root. `existsSync` refuses a missing store BEFORE any open, so no ledger is ever created implicitly; verified by real run, `ABSENT_CREATED=false`.
- IMPORT-SHADOW UNTOUCHED: `git diff --numstat HEAD -- tools/import/import-shadow.ts tools/import/shadow-input.ts tools/import/shadow-input.js` prints NOTHING. Zero bytes moved; the read-only posture and DISCARDING_STORE are exactly as they were.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: PLACEMENT was the one real decision; the adapter itself is deliberately trivial. Chose tools/import/import-commit.ts as a sibling of import-shadow.ts. REJECTED: (a) inside packages/import -- the task rail forbids @moe/import depending on @moe/store, and the port abstraction exists precisely so the package never sees a concrete store; (b) inside apps/daemon behind a command -- zero @moe/import references exist in the daemon today, the command vocabulary is frozen with a full-coverage ratchet, and inventing `import.commit` as a kind is a far larger authority decision than this producer-gap task may smuggle; the task rail explicitly says 'if the durable write belongs behind a daemon command, place it there' -- I considered it and the answer is not yet: cutover/activation tasks own that decision, and this task only needs the drafted events to become durable rows on a REAL import path, which a CLI entry satisfies; (c) modifying import-shadow.ts to take a --write flag -- its read-only posture is asserted on BYTES in its own header and rail-protected; a write mode would invalidate its central guarantee. The adapter maps ImportCommitInput to the store's CommitInput field-for-field -- the shapes are already compatible (measured, not assumed), and ImportEventDraft's REQUIRED domainSchemaVersion exists precisely because the store's EventDraft defaults it; the adapter must pass it through explicitly, never spread-with-defaults. The conflict-path subtlety drove test design: applyImport wraps THROWN commit failures as IMPORT_COMMIT_FAILED/APPLY, so if SqliteEventStore.commit throws on version conflict the adapter must catch and surface the store's code as a typed answer rather than letting it be restamped -- DoD 4 demands the store's own code and layer survive verbatim.

planningNotes.risks: The defining risk is an adapter that quietly transforms: a defensive copy that re-encodes a payload, a spread that lets the store default domainSchemaVersion, or an added bookkeeping event would all commit successfully and read back plausibly -- only byte-identity and exact-count assertions catch them, which is why DoD 3's two mutations are drills 1 and 2 and why the decode assertion has its own vacuity drill (a sweep decoding zero claims passes while proving nothing, DoD 5's explicit worry). Second, restamping: a version conflict surfacing as IMPORT_COMMIT_FAILED erases the distinction DoD 4 requires -- the adapter must let the store's own conflict code/layer survive, and the test must pin WHICH layer answered, since applyImport's catch-all sits one frame above. Third, the read-only posture of import-shadow.ts is a guarantee asserted on bytes -- change nothing there, and prove zero-byte diff at review. Fourth, tools/ files are typechecked ONLY via explicit enumeration in the typecheck:import script; forgetting to add the new file leaves it typechecked by nothing and green forever. Fifth, dependency direction: packages/import must gain no @moe/store import -- the whole port design exists to keep that edge out. Sixth, the CLI must fail closed on a missing store path rather than creating one -- an implicitly-created empty store would make the duplicate-manifest test meaningless and could silently write authority rows in a wrong directory. Finally, close every store handle on every path; a held SQLite handle kills the vitest worker.
